channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Cooperation With UN Secretary-General
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek. Guterres congratulated Uzbekistan on its 35th independence anniversary. They discussed expanding cooperation with the UN and its institutions, and Guterres welcomed Uzbekistan's achievements in Sustainable Development Goals.

item.title: Uzbek President and Chinese President Discuss Strengthening Comprehensive Cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Bishkek during the SCO summit. Mirziyoyev thanked Xi for congratulations on Uzbekistan's independence anniversary and contributions to bilateral relations. They proposed a program to celebrate the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties next year and noted trade turnover nearing $18 billion.

item.title: Uzbek President Arrives in Bishkek for SCO Summit and 'SCO Plus' Meeting
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has arrived in Bishkek to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Council of Heads of State meeting and an 'SCO Plus' format meeting. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport by Kyrgyz officials and is scheduled for bilateral meetings and the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expand Cooperation with UN; President Mirziyoyev Meets António Guterres in Bishkek
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to expand its cooperation with the United Nations. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres in Bishkek to exchange views on pressing issues. The meeting took place during the SCO summit.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China agree to boost trade to $30 billion
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in Bishkek, agreeing to increase bilateral trade to $30 billion in the coming years. Current trade is near $18 billion. They also discussed joint investment projects worth $60 billion, focusing on energy, mining, and transport, including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway.

item.title: Russia and China may make visa-free travel regime permanent
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated Russia is ready to work with China to make their visa-free travel regime permanent. Putin expressed readiness to continue cooperation on this issue with the Chinese side. Both leaders are in Kyrgyzstan for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit and the World Nomad Games.

item.title: Bishkek summit to test SCO's economic ambitions, media reports
item.description: The Bishkek summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation will focus on advancing the SCO Development Bank, Development Fund, and Investment Fund. Al Jazeera notes that Kyrgyzstan, during its presidency, prioritized establishing these financial institutions. The meeting's success will depend on transitioning from political statements to practical agreements on funding mechanisms and capital sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China leaders discuss boosting trade to $30 billion
item.description: During a meeting in Kyrgyzstan, the leaders of Uzbekistan and China discussed various issues, including a proposal to increase bilateral trade volume from the current $18 billion to $30 billion. The leaders engaged in discussions on multiple aspects of their bilateral relationship.

item.title: Russia and China may permanently abolish visa requirements
item.description: Russia is ready to permanently transition to a visa-free regime with China, stated Russian President Vladimir Putin during a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Bishkek. Both leaders are in Kyrgyzstan to attend the SCO summit and the World Nomad Games opening ceremony.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Iran leaders discuss energy cooperation and new transport routes
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Bishkek to discuss bilateral relations, focusing on trade, energy cooperation, and expanding transport and logistics. They also addressed cultural ties and international issues on the sidelines of the SCO Summit.

item.title: Russian President Putin arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit to attend the 6th World Nomad Games and the SCO Heads of State Council meeting. He will also hold bilateral talks with several leaders and Russia will assume the SCO presidency in 2027-2028.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes New System for Preserving Memory of Victims of Repression
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed developing a new system to preserve the memory of victims of political repression and those who died for the country. He noted the expansion of efforts to immortalize victims' memories, including publishing books and holding events.

item.title: Turkish President Erdogan Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for Working Visit
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine Erdogan, arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit. They were welcomed at Manas International Airport by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. Erdogan is scheduled to hold bilateral talks with several heads of state in Bishkek.

item.title: Kyrgyz and Mongolian Presidents Discuss Joint Projects and Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh to discuss strengthening bilateral ties. They emphasized building on shared heritage to develop concrete trade, economic, investment, and transport projects for mutual benefit.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes expanding cooperation with India in pharmaceuticals and IT
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to discuss trade, investment, and healthcare cooperation. Japarov highlighted education, medicine, pharmaceuticals, and IT as key areas. Both leaders agreed to elevate bilateral ties.

item.title: Ukraine may strike Russia using Starlink, Zelensky asked Musk for permission
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reportedly asked Elon Musk for permission to use Starlink-equipped drones against Russian targets up to 200 kilometers inside Russian territory. The Financial Times reported this, citing sources familiar with the matter.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit to attend the SCO Heads of State Council meeting, a high-level "SCO plus" meeting, and the opening ceremony of the Nomad Games. He was welcomed by the head of the cabinet of ministers at Manas International Airport. Kyrgyzstan will chair the SCO in 2026.

item.title: Tajikistan's National Bank to Pilot E-Wallet Taxation from September 1
item.description: Tajikistan's National Bank announced a three-month pilot program for taxing individual entrepreneurs via e-wallets, starting September 1. The system aims to tax business transactions through e-wallets, with a previously proposed rate of 3% (down from 6%). Further details on specific transaction limits are pending. The bank is collaborating with innovation agencies and tax authorities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Showcases Crafts at Venice's Homo Faber Exhibition
item.description: Uzbekistan is participating in the fourth edition of the Homo Faber 2026: An Island of Light exhibition in Venice, showcasing contemporary artistic craftsmanship. Organized by the Michelangelo Foundation, the event features over 700 artworks from 500 artisans worldwide. Uzbekistan's participation is supported by the Foundation for Development of Culture and Arts, which began collaborating with Michelangelo Foundation in 2022.

item.title: Russian strikes disrupt power supply in six Ukrainian regions, causing casualties
item.description: New Russian strikes on Ukraine have disrupted electricity supply in six regions: Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Sumy, and Mykolaiv. Emergency repair work is underway where security permits. In Kherson, two people died and two were injured following drone attacks on a medical facility and the city center.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon discusses cooperation and regional security with US representatives
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon met with US Special Envoy for Central and South Asia Sergio Gor and Senator Steve Daines in Bishkek. They discussed cooperation, trade, investment in energy and mining, and regional security and stability, emphasizing the C5+1 platform.

item.title: Kazakhstan's economy ends summer with growth but facing high inflation and credit costs
item.description: Kazakhstan's economy grew 4.1% in January-July, driven by construction and transport, despite a decline in oil production. However, inflation reached 10.2% year-on-year in July, and credit remains expensive. The number of small and medium enterprises decreased by 8%.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev arrives in Bishkek for SCO summit and expanded format meeting
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has arrived in Bishkek to participate in the upcoming meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and a meeting in the SCO Plus format.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev arrives in Bishkek with his wife for SCO meeting and games opening
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, accompanied by his wife, has arrived in Bishkek for the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting and SCO Plus format meeting. He will hold bilateral meetings and attend the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan replaces its ambassador to Tajikistan
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has appointed Nazarali Oripov as the new ambassador to Tajikistan. Oripov replaces Erlan Abdildaev, who served as ambassador since April 2022 and was dismissed in July. Abdildaev has since been appointed ambassador to Hungary.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Japarov Seeks Easing of US Visa Bond Requirements
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan met with U.S. Special Envoy Sergio Gor to discuss simplifying visa requirements for Kyrgyz citizens traveling to the United States. They specifically addressed reviewing the visa bond requirement and other restrictions. Gor expressed readiness to strengthen Kyrgyzstan-USA relations and discussed political dialogue, trade, and investment cooperation.

item.title: SCO Summit and State Visits to Bishkek: Developments Today
item.description: Bishkek is hosting events related to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit and official visits by heads of state on August 31 and September 1, expecting 21 presidents and prime ministers. Unprecedented security measures are in place. The SCO marks its 25th anniversary, with the summit on September 1. Meetings between Armenian and Azerbaijani leaders, and the arrival of the Pakistani Prime Minister are noted.

item.title: Armenian PM Pashinyan Reports Meeting with Azerbaijani President Aliyev in Bishkek
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announced on social media that he met with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Bishkek. Pashinyan shared footage of the negotiations. Further details about the meeting and the topics discussed were not immediately available. Both leaders are in Kyrgyzstan to attend the SCO Plus high-level meeting and the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games.

item.title: Afghanistan does not pose a threat to neighboring countries, says Taliban representative
item.description: A representative of Afghanistan's interim government, Zabihullah Mujahid, responded to statements about supplying weapons to the Tajikistan-Afghanistan border. Mujahid stated that Afghanistan does not pose a threat to its neighbors. This statement comes after reports of an agreement to strengthen the border.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sees Togo as a key partner in Africa, president says
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov met with Togo's Prime Minister, noting that Togo is a promising partner on the African continent. Japarov thanked Togo for supporting Kyrgyzstan's bid for a non-permanent UN Security Council seat. Togo expressed interest in expanding trade, economic, and cultural cooperation.

item.title: Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon arrives in Kyrgyzstan for working visit
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan arrived in Kyrgyzstan on August 31 for a working visit. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. Rahmon will attend the SCO summit and the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games.

item.title: Kazakhstan's healthcare and social services exceed one trillion tenge in Q2 2026
item.description: In the second quarter of 2026, healthcare and social service organizations in Kazakhstan provided services worth over 1.05 trillion tenge. The Social Health Insurance Fund (FSMС) covered nearly half of this amount. Hospital organizations accounted for the largest share of services provided.

item.title: Pakistan Culture Days to be held in Tajikistan in 2027
item.description: Pakistan Culture Days will take place in Tajikistan in 2027 as part of cultural cooperation. The event aims to introduce Tajikistan's residents to Pakistani culture, art, and literature. Meetings with cultural representatives and exhibitions are planned.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev travels to Bishkek for SCO Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has departed for Bishkek on a working visit. He will attend the upcoming meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) and a "SCO Plus" format meeting on August 31.

item.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Calls US Economic War Against Tehran a "Failed Policy"
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described US President Donald Trump's threat to initiate an economic war against Tehran as a continuation of Washington's "failed policies." This statement criticizes the US approach to economic pressure on Iran.

item.title: Yerlan Karin Appointed Vice President of Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree appointing Yerlan Karin as the country's Vice President. The appointment follows parliamentary approval, with 141 out of 145 deputies supporting Karin's nomination. This new role was established under the new constitution.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Arrives in Bishkek for SCO Summit
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. He was welcomed at the airport by Kyrgyzstan's acting Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev and other officials. The presidential press service reported on the arrival.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes New Funding Rules for Private Schools
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Education has proposed new rules for funding private schools that operate under the state order. The ministry suggests establishing a fixed funding amount, independent of the annual increase in the monthly calculated indicator (MRP), to ensure educational accessibility and stability.

item.title: Infrastructure Development Fund Established as Treasury Account in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Infrastructure Development Fund will operate as a special account within the state treasury, rather than a separate organization. This fund will finance major national infrastructure projects, with payments disbursed in stages based on work completion, as reported by Orda.kz.

item.title: China proposes 'Water Silk Road' via Irtysh River for Arctic access
item.description: China, Kazakhstan, and Russia are discussing a project to transform the Irtysh River into a cargo corridor with Arctic access, dubbed the 'Water Silk Road'. This route, originating in China and flowing through Kazakhstan and Russia to the Arctic Ocean, could offer China an alternative to vulnerable maritime routes. Infrastructure development, including dams and dredging, would be necessary.
